title: The Unquiet Will
premise: Wendell Villalobos, the coroner of salt-worn Port Isla, identifies a drowned stranger wearing clothes lifted from his own closet — and finds a page of a coded ledger sewn into the lining. The ledger, kept for decades by the town's founding families, records debts of identity: names bought, sold, and buried. As Wendell decodes it with help from Marisol, the witness who found the body and the only person who ever truly saw him, he discovers the dead man was hired to deliver Wendell's true birth record to someone who wants him erased. In the climax at the tide flats, Wendell confronts the town matriarch who purchased his name forty years ago, choosing love and chosen family over the duty of silence; the ledger burns, but Wendell keeps one page — his own.
about_author: Ansel Reyes is the pen name of a former coastal-town archivist who spent years cataloguing unclaimed estates and the letters people never sent. They write mysteries about small places that keep large secrets.

chapters.title: The Borrowed Coat
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. A body washes up at Gull Point wearing Wendell's own missing coat, and the witness, Marisol Quintero, swears she saw the man alive wearing it days earlier. Wendell's autopsy reveals a stitched page of ciphered numbers in the lining. Emotional beat: uncanny violation — the intimacy of being dressed in your own death.

chapters.title: Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: POV Wendell, alternating with Marisol's account. Together they crack the cipher: a generational ledger of bought identities maintained by the Delacruz family, with Wendell's childhood name appearing as an entry marked 'settled.' Someone begins searching Wendell's office. Emotional beat: vertigo — the self he trusted as solid turns out to be a purchase.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: POV Marisol. She admits she recognized the dead man — a courier her family once used — and hid it out of fear. The Delacruz matriarch, Odile, summons Wendell, offering him his 'real' history in exchange for the ledger page. He refuses; that night his office burns. Emotional beat: love against duty — Wendell and Marisol choose each other over safety.

chapters.title: The Unquiet Will
chapters.summary: POV Wendell. At low tide on the flats, Wendell confronts Odile, who confesses she bought his name to settle her brother's death decades ago — the courier was her last loose end. Marisol arrives with the sheriff; Odile surrenders rather than let the sea take another. Wendell keeps his single page and buries the courier under his own recovered name. Emotional beat: resolution — identity claimed, not inherited.
